logistic_model_gap.statement: Need to fit logistic regression with specific optimization procedure (gradient descent 200 iter, lr=0.1) and evaluate across 5-fold CV, interaction features, and model compression

hyp_l2_regularization.statement: L2 regularization will improve generalization; some intermediate lambda value (0.01-1.0) should outperform both unregularized (0.0) and heavily regularized (10.0) baselines

hyp_interaction_features.statement: Interaction features may provide additional predictive signal; paired t-test across folds will reveal if improvements exceed noise threshold (t > 2.0)

hyp_model_compression.statement: Some combination of sparsity and quantization can be applied without severely degrading performance; retention metric will identify the optimal trade-off

claim_best_lambda.statement: 5-fold CV with gradient descent (200 iter, lr=0.1) on logistic regression: best lambda is 0.1 with mean Brier 0.207077, improving 0.00890 over unregularized baseline (Brier 0.215977)

claim_interactions.statement: Adding interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) significantly reduces Brier score across 5 folds with lambda=0.1; paired t-test t-stat=3.91 (p=0.017) exceeds threshold t>2.0, so interaction_helps=true

claim_compression.statement: Best model compression config is sparsity20_bits4 with retention 0.999222; this configuration zeros 20% of smallest-magnitude weights and quantizes remainder to 2^4=16 levels, retaining nearly full performance
